heroTitle:
We preserve
towers. We uncover
the world’s stories.
heroLead: Every water tower embodies an engineering breakthrough, architectural identity, and generations of memories. IMWT connects them in an open digital museum accessible to everyone.
heroProof: Open heritage. Verifiable sources. Shared responsibility.
missionText: We usually tell civilization’s story through palaces, temples and bridges. Yet water towers shaped everyday life too: they helped cities expand, industries operate and communities access reliable water supplies.
missionText2: IMWT studies this engineering legacy, its impact on cities and society, and the tower as an early symbol of complex urban networks. Direct links to later technologies are research questions, not established historical conclusions.
value1Text: Find water towers even when their history lives only in the memories of local residents.
value2Text: Collect documents, plans, memories, technologies and the names of their creators.
value3Text: Make knowledge accessible and help communities imagine a new future for their towers.
atlasDesc: An open digital encyclopedia envisioned for towers from different countries, periods and construction traditions. For now, this is a visual prototype.
atlasNote: Concept map only. The public registry is in development; these markers are not verified entries in a global database.
researchTitle:
More than structures.
Living archives of civilization.
researchAside: For every tower, we want to understand far more than its address and construction date: we want to tell its fullest possible story.
research1Text: Tanks, hydraulics, pressure, materials, equipment, structural systems and upgrades.
research2Text: Attribution, plans, design schools, builders and the history of engineering creativity.
research3Text: Local names, oral testimony, myths, family photographs and cultural context.
research4Text: Restoration, adaptive reuse, museums and sustainable preservation models.
pilotText: A historic water tower in Mala Vilshanka, Kyiv region, will be IMWT’s starting point: the site of the first exhibition, pilot research and experimentation with digital museum formats.
pilotDisclaimer: The site is being prepared for future development. Public opening is subject to surveys, design reviews and all necessary approvals.
contributeTitle:
Know a water tower?
Tell us its story.
contributeDesc: Residents, architects, researchers, owners, companies and municipal authorities can propose an object for the international research archive. No registration. No fee.
step1Text: Its name, location, approximate age, condition and memorable details.
step2Text: Photographs, scans, documents or a shared archive link.
step3Text: Our team checks sources and may contact you. Submission does not mean automatic publication.
uploadNote: You can upload up to three files totaling 8 MB per submission. For larger collections, share a cloud-folder link. Do not submit sensitive operational plans or personal data without authorization.
towerFormSub: Your contribution to global engineering history
labelStory: History, facts, legends and engineering details *
labelArchive: Archive or Google Drive folder link
consentTower: I confirm that I am authorized to submit these materials for editorial review and consent to processing my contact details for follow-up. Publication requires separate rights verification.
supportTitle:
Protecting heritage
takes all of us.
supportDesc: We invite philanthropists, foundations, businesses, museums, universities, municipalities and communities to collaborate. Help build a global open knowledge base and support the future preservation of towers.
supportCaution: Online payments are not active yet. Leave your details and the IMWT team will contact you to discuss a secure, legally structured way to support the initiative.
partnerFormSub: Leave your details and we will contact you
consentPartner: I consent to processing the contact details provided solely to respond to my IMWT inquiry.
noPayment: No payment is processed by this form.
timeline1Text: Website, public submissions, international outreach and organizational setup.
timeline2Text: Documentation standards, source verification, pilot catalog and digital exhibitions.
timeline3Text: Design work, safety assessments and phased exhibition development in Mala Vilshanka.
timeline4Text: Collaboration with cities, museums and researchers, plus heritage preservation programs.
closingTitle:
The world forgets towers.
We’ll preserve their stories.
closingText: One photograph, one document or one memory can start a major discovery.
footerAbout: An international initiative to preserve and document the world’s water towers. Starting in Ukraine.
histTitle: History of the world’s water towers — from the 1st century BC to the 21st century
histText: From Pompeii and Mimar Sinan to Shukhov, Poelzig and Torroja: the oldest surviving towers of 9 European countries, 29 architects and engineers, 87 sources, 22 photographs, Ukrainian towers, wars and memory — told by the water tower in Mala Vilshanka. Available in English and Ukrainian.
uaTitle: Water towers of Ukraine — an illustrated atlas, 1866–2026
uaText: 40 dossiers from the Kachanivka estate and Kyiv’s first waterworks to Shukhov’s towers in Mykolaiv and Cherkasy, Lviv functionalism and post-war towers: dates, architects, engineers, clients, heritage status and 37 photographs. Narrated by the water tower in Mala Vilshanka. Available in English and Ukrainian.
wpAside: The research concept, a digital encyclopedia of the world’s engineering heritage, and the museum’s development program — in one open document.
wpDocTitle: International Museum of Water Towers: research concept, digital encyclopedia of global engineering heritage, and development program
